title: Cadwalader to Merge with Hogan Lovells, Creating Historic Law Firm Powerhouse
author: Staci Zaretsky

dom.t: Big Law economics: Durable value exceeds firm size

mo.t: Big Four: Integration matters more than replacement
Big Law economics: Durable value exceeds firm size
Workflow unbundling: Buyers challenge time-based production

kp.k: Merger extends access to existing AI infrastructure
kp.d: The July 2026 BeBeez appendix predicts that the merger will accelerate the combined firm's leadership in AI-powered legal services, with Cadwalader benefiting from Hogan Lovells' joint venture ELTEMATE and proprietary chatbot CRAIG. It reports that CRAIG already supports over 4,400 users, but provides no measured effects on productivity, staffing, pricing or service quality.
qs: The merger will accelerate Hogan Lovells Cadwalader's leadership in AI-powered legal services.
Cadwalader will benefit from Hogan Lovells' joint venture, **ELTEMATE, and its proprietary chatbot, CRAIG**, which already supports over 4,400 users.

kp.k: Announced combination becomes a completed global merger
kp.d: The December 18, 2025 article anticipates a 2026 closing, about 3,100 lawyers and the world's fifth-largest firm by revenue. The July 3, 2026 appendix subsequently reports completion, April 2026 partner approval and July 1 rebranding as Hogan Lovells Cadwalader. Its updated scale figures are over 3,200 lawyers, over 900 partners, turnover above 3.6 billion US dollars and presence in more than 18 countries. These describe market consolidation; the document does not attribute the merger's formation to AI.
qs: The prospective tie-up is expected to be the largest law firm merger in history, and will close sometime in 2026.
The combined firm, Hogan Lovells Cadwalader, will have about 3,100 lawyers spread across the globe, with clientele in every major financial market.
The new firm will become an absolute financial powerhouse — the world's fifth-largest firm by revenue, in fact — with gross revenue of more than $3.6 billion.
after having completed the merger that was announced in December 2025 and the partners approved in April 2026.
HLC has over 3,200 lawyers across the Americas, EMEA and APAC, a turnover of above 3.6 billion US dollars, over 900 partners and a presence in more than 18 countries.

kp.k: Reported financial compatibility supports the merger rationale
kp.d: Quoting The American Lawyer's use of Am Law 100 data, the article describes moderately similar revenue per lawyer and average profits per equity partner despite substantial differences in total revenue. For 2024, Hogan Lovells had $2.964 billion in revenue versus Cadwalader's $638.2 million; revenue per lawyer was $1.097 million versus $1.495 million, and average equity-partner profits were $3.072 million versus $3.709 million. These are merger-context financial comparisons, not evidence of AI-driven gains.
qs: According to Am Law 100 data, Cadwalader and Hogan Lovells have moderately similar revenue per lawyer and average profits per equity partner.
Hogan Lovells brought in $2.964 billion in revenue in 2024, more than quadruple the amount of revenue Cadwalader brought in at $638.2 million.
In RPL, Hogan earned $1.097 million while Cadwalader generated $1.495 million, a $398,000 difference.
Meanwhile, Hogan's average PEP came in at $3.072 million, whereas Cadwalader generated $3.709 million, just over $600,000 in difference.

kp.k: Cadwalader's partner departures precede its merger announcement
kp.d: Zaretsky characterizes Cadwalader as distressed and reports rapid departures of key partner groups following its deal with Donald Trump. She places the Hogan Lovells announcement after reported merger talks with Alston & Bird one month earlier. This is the author's account of the consolidation backdrop, rather than an AI-related explanation of lawyer departures.
qs: In the wake of the firm's deal with Donald Trump, the firm started losing lawyers left and right, with key partner groups lateraling out at a rapid pace.
Rumors of the firm's interest in a merger began to spread, and just one month ago, we reported that Cadwalader was in merger talks with Atlanta-based Alston & Bird.

kp.k: Leaders emphasize client complexity and cultural compatibility
kp.d: In the completion appendix, CEO Miguel A. Zaldivar, Jr. presents the combination as responding to clients seeking advice on complex issues in major G20 economies. Global managing partner Pat Quinn identifies cultural compatibility and integration of practices and clients as important to merger success and immediate client benefits. These are leadership statements of rationale and expected benefits, not independently measured outcomes.
qs: We continue to build on these strengths whilst paying close attention to the evolving needs of our clients, who are increasingly seeking advisers capable of guiding them through the most complex issues in the major G20 economies.
The journey that led us to this achievement highlighted the importance of cultural compatibility for the success of this merger.
We took an accurate approach to integrating our practices and clients to ensure that, right from day one, our clients can benefit fully from the new platform we created.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: The BeBeez International appendix predicts that the merger will accelerate the combined firm's leadership in AI-powered legal services, with Cadwalader benefiting from Hogan Lovells' existing AI resources.
pts.d: This prediction appears in the appendix's reporting, not in Staci Zaretsky's original article or in the quoted executive statements. The resources identified are Hogan Lovells' joint venture ELTEMATE and its proprietary chatbot CRAIG. The source does not specify which legal tasks will change or predict measurable effects on productivity, service quality, pricing or employment.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The supporting basis is the existence of ELTEMATE and CRAIG and a reported existing user base of over 4,400.
pts.d: The appendix supplies an adoption figure as context for the predicted benefit. It provides no benchmark, measured service improvement or comparative evidence establishing AI leadership or demonstrating how the merger will accelerate it. The user figure is reported by the appendix without a stated measurement method.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The AI benefits are prospective following the reported July 2026 merger completion; CRAIG's user base is described as already existing.
pts.d: The appendix, dated 3 July 2026, reports completion and rebranding on 1 July. Its AI prediction is framed as a consequence of the combination, with no specific delivery deadline or additional conditions stated. The original December 2025 article contains no AI prediction.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The explicitly identified beneficiaries are the combined firm and Cadwalader.
pts.d: The combined firm is predicted to strengthen its position in AI-powered legal services, while Cadwalader is predicted to benefit from Hogan Lovells' AI resources. Although the appendix reports CRAIG's existing users, it does not identify their roles or organisations. It does not specify AI-related effects on particular clients, practice areas, junior lawyers, other staff or the public.
